teal-ink.purpose: Long-form reading text on cream only (notes, descriptions). Never on rose.

urgent.purpose: Overdue chores, high priority, error text.

ok.purpose: On track, low priority, success feedback.

title.purpose: Card headers, chore names, todo titles.

body.purpose: List content, metadata, descriptions. Teal ink on cream.

label.purpose: Filter buttons, tag text, form labels. Always bold.

shadows.name: ambient
shadows.purpose: Calendar day cells and structural separation.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Nav button hover and interactive element activation.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Quint out: arrivals and state changes.

motion.name: ease-screen
motion.purpose: Screen pushes: moves at once, lands softly.

motion.name: swap
motion.value: background-color, color, border-color, box-shadow 130ms ease-out; transform 100ms ease-out

motion.name: page-transition
motion.value: Horizontal push View Transition: leaving screen translates out, next translates in beside it, 360ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.8, 0.25, 1), in nav order (forms sit right of their tab); nav pill glides in step
motion.purpose: Screens arrive whole: tabs stay mounted and refresh in place, background tabs warm up after first load, a not-yet-loaded tab holds the change up to 600ms.

motion.name: dialog
motion.value: enter: opacity 0→1, translate 12px→0, scale .98→1, 200ms ease-out; exit 130ms ease-in
motion.purpose: Native dialog open/close via @starting-style and modalDialog.

motion.name: list
motion.value: flip 260ms ease-out; reveal 200ms (6px rise); vanish 130ms fade

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action. Rose fill, cream text. Hover inverts to cream/rose.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { padding: 8px 14px; border-radius: 7px; border: solid 2px #8F5C66; background-color: #8F5C66; color: #FFEAD0; font-weight: bold; cursor: pointer; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', 'Franklin Gothic', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background-color: #FFEAD0; color: #8F5C66; text-decoration: underline; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action. Cream fill, rose text. Same border as primary — only fill swaps.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { padding: 8px 14px; border-radius: 7px; border: solid 2px #8F5C66; background-color: #FFEAD0; color: #8F5C66; cursor: pointer; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', 'Franklin Gothic', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background-color: #8F5C66; color: #FFEAD0; text-decoration: underline; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive action only (delete). The one red button. Hover inverts.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { width: 100%; padding: 13px; border-radius: 7px; border: solid 2px #C71414; background-color: #C71414; color: #FFEAD0; font-weight: bold; cursor: pointer; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', 'Franklin Gothic', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 1.05rem; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out, color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background-color: #FFEAD0; color: #C71414; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #7A4E56; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Nav Button
components.description: Top navigation tab. Active state is the inverted (cream) variant.
components.css: .ds-btn-nav { border: 2px solid #8F5C66; border-radius: 7px; cursor: pointer; height: 3rem; font-weight: bold; font-size: clamp(12px, 2vw, 32px); background-color: #8F5C66; color: #FFEAD0; padding: 0 12px; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', 'Franklin Gothic', Arial, sans-serif; transition: background-color 0.2s, color 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-btn-nav:hover, .ds-btn-nav.ds-active { background-color: #FFEAD0; color: #8F5C66; box-shadow: 0 7px 15px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); }

components.name: Tag / Chip
components.description: Room and category filter. Cream at rest, rose on hover/active.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 5px 12px; border-radius: 999px; border: solid 2px #8F5C66; background-color: #FFEAD0; color: #8F5C66; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.9em; cursor: pointer; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', 'Franklin Gothic', Arial, sans-serif; transition: background-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-tag:hover, .ds-tag.ds-active { background-color: #8F5C66; color: #FFEAD0; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Todo and chore item card. Rose header band bleeds to edges; cream body.
components.html:
Take out trash

Due today · Kitchen
components.css: .ds-card { border-radius: 10px; border: solid 2px #8F5C66; background-color: #FFEAD0; color: #8F5C66; display: flex; flex-direction: column; padding: 10px; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.3s; overflow: hidden; } .ds-card:hover { transform: scale(1.02); } .ds-card-header { font-size: 1.2em; font-weight: bold; background-color: #8F5C66; color: #FFEAD0; border-radius: 5px 5px 0 0; padding: 0.75em 1em; margin: -10px -10px 10px -10px; } .ds-card-body { margin: 0; font-size: 0.9em; color: #8F5C66; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Inline text field. Underline-only style; no background, no outer border.
components.css: .ds-input { outline: none; background: none; border: none; border-bottom: 2px solid #8F5C66; border-radius: 0; caret-color: rgba(143, 92, 102,0.5); color: #8F5C66; padding: 4px 2px; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', 'Franklin Gothic', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 1em; transition: border-color 0.2s; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #7a4e56; }

components.name: Collapsible Trigger
components.description: Full-width section expander. Rose bg with underline text; inverts on hover.
components.css: .ds-collapsible { width: 100%; border: solid #8F5C66 2px; border-radius: 7px; padding: 10px; text-align: left; font-size: 16px; cursor: pointer; text-decoration: underline; background-color: #8F5C66; color: #FFEAD0; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', 'Franklin Gothic', Arial, sans-serif; transition: background-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-collapsible:hover { background-color: #FFEAD0; color: #8F5C66; }

components.name: FAB
components.description: Fixed floating action button. Circle shape, cream/rose at rest, inverts on hover.
components.css: .ds-fab { height: clamp(50px, 10vh, 80px); width: clamp(50px, 10vh, 80px); cursor: pointer; font-size: clamp(20px, 5vh, 48px); background-color: #FFEAD0; color: #8F5C66; border: 2px solid #8F5C66; border-radius: 50%; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', 'Franklin Gothic', Arial, sans-serif; transition: background-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-fab:hover { background-color: #8F5C66; color: #FFEAD0; }

components.name: Nav Bar
components.description: Full-width top navigation bar containing evenly spaced nav buttons.
components.html: <nav class="ds-navbar"><button class="ds-btn-nav">Home</button><button class="ds-btn-nav ds-active">Calendar</button><button class="ds-btn-nav">Chores</button><button class="ds-btn-nav">Todo</button></nav>

narrative.overview:
This system reads like a household almanac kept on the kitchen shelf: a dependable printed reference with a seasonal rhythm. Entries are ruled and orderly, the paper is warm, the ink is a single faded rose. It is consulted in seconds ("what's today, who's on it") and trusted because its structure never changes from page to page. Not a digital product imitating paper, but one that shares print's values: legibility first, warmth through material, structure that feels earned.

The color discipline is strict: two voices do all the work. Dusty rose and warm cream form a closed system, and the primary interaction is always a clean inversion between them. Rose is the ink: text, borders, headers, active fills. Shadows appear only when earned by interaction; everything else is flat. Density is low. Household members glance at this app between tasks; they do not sit and study it.

Motion is quick, continuous, and calm. Tabs are peers, so they fade through in place while the nav pill glides to its new tab; forms rise from below and settle back; the masthead never moves. Nothing pops into place and nothing jumps; lists close their gaps, panels unfold, and late data eases in. Motion starts almost at once (under 100ms after a tap), every movement is short (100 to 260ms) and decelerates softly, and all of it disappears for anyone who prefers reduced motion.

Every household member re-inks their own almanac: each person picks a two-colour theme in Settings, and it follows them to every device. A theme swaps only the two voices (`--primary` and `--paper`); every other colour derives from them, structure never changes, and every palette keeps the AA contrast the default guarantees.

This system explicitly refuses: Google's over-minimalism (stripped to nothing), generic SaaS white-and-blue (this lives in a home, not an office), dense productivity tools like Jira and Asana (wrong register entirely), and the pastel Cozi-style "family app" look (too soft, not enough structure).
keyCharacteristics: Two-voice palette: dusty rose + warm cream, inverted on every interaction
Rose is the ink: text on cream is rose at 4.6:1 (AA)
Flat at rest; shadows as feedback, never decoration
One typeface (Libre Franklin); hierarchy through weight and a 1.2 size scale
Gently curved corners on a fixed 5 / 7 / 10 px scale
Every value is a token, so households can re-theme without breaking anything
Continuous motion: nothing pops or jumps; things arrive with a soft deceleration and leave quickly

rules.name: The Two-Colour Theme Rule
rules.body: A palette is exactly two colours, and must keep primary/paper at 4.5:1 or more (the UI inverts them on hover) and teal ink at 11:1 or more on the paper. Avoid red, orange, or green-leaning primaries that would blur into the status colours. Components never name a palette colour: they read `--primary` and `--paper`.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: The primary interaction pattern is a full color swap: rose flips to cream, cream flips to rose. No gradients, no intermediate tints, no opacity tricks. A hover that does anything else needs a strong reason.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Page surfaces speak rose and cream only. Teal ink appears only in paragraphs. Delete red appears on destructive actions alone; using it elsewhere devalues it.

rules.name: The Solid Ink Rule
rules.body: Text is never alpha-tinted. Cream at 60% on rose is 2.7:1 and rose at 45% on cream is 1.8:1; both fail. Secondary text gets hierarchy from size, weight, or italic in a solid color, never from opacity. Alpha tints (`--primary-a08` to `--primary-a45`, `--paper-a12` to `--paper-a60`) are for washes, tracks, and hairlines only.

rules.name: The Never-Hue-Alone Rule
rules.body: Status color always travels with a label, icon, or position. Warn (2.5:1), ok (3.4:1), and muted (1.7:1) are too light to carry meaning by themselves, and a household theme may shift them anyway.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: One font, all roles. Hierarchy lives in weight (`--weight-regular` 400 / `--weight-bold` 700, nothing between) and the 1.2 size scale. Do not add a second typeface for visual interest; the color system already does that work.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Font sizes are `var(--text-*)`, never px, em, or a one-off rem. Fluid `clamp()` type is prohibited in UI (the FAB glyph is the one exception, sized with its button). A size that doesn't fit the scale is a design question, not a new value.

rules.name: The Theme Hook Rule
rules.body: Components read `--font-sans`, never a family name, so a household theme can swap the face without touching components.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A permanent shadow needs a structural reason (separation from content beneath). Decorative shadows are prohibited. If a card at rest casts a shadow, remove it.

rules.name: The Whole-Word Rule
rules.body: On every screen down to 320px, words never split and short labels (times, buttons, chips, names, nav labels) never wrap; groups of them wrap as whole items. Nothing may be wider than the screen, because on a phone one overflow makes the whole page pan sideways. Hover styles live inside @media (hover: hover), so taps never leave a control looking pressed.

dos: Do use the rose/cream inversion as the hover and active pattern everywhere. Consistency is the system.
Do read every color, radius, border, and shadow from `tokens.css`. A hardcoded hex breaks household theming.
Do size text only with `--text-xs` to `--text-xl` and weight only with 400/700.
Do keep text on cream in solid dusty rose (#8F5C66, 4.6:1) and paragraphs in teal ink (#113537).
Do rely on the global `:focus-visible` outline; add `.on-primary` to primary-filled containers so it turns paper-coloured there. Never write `outline: none`.
Do pair every status color with a label, icon, or position.
Do keep surfaces flat at rest; add the lift shadow only on hover for interactive elements.
Do use the radius scale: 10px panels, cards, dialogs; 7px buttons, inputs, list rows; 5px dense tiles and calendar pills; pills for chips and badges.
Do use 2px borders on every bordered control and container; 1px hairlines only for dividers and dense grids.
Do lead each screen with what the household came to check (today, overdue, whose turn), per PRODUCT.md's "glance first".
Do check every screen at 320px and 360px wide: no word split, no short label wrapped, nothing past the edge.
donts: Don't use generic SaaS white-and-blue. "This lives in someone's home, not an office."
Don't drift toward Google's over-minimalism. Clean is good; stripped to nothing is not.
Don't build dense Jira/Asana-style screens: no toolbars of twelve icons, no 13px data grids.
Don't use the pastel Cozi-style "family app" look: no baby blue, no gradient backgrounds, no rounded-everything with drop shadows.
Don't tint text with alpha or use idle gray (2.3:1) for readable text.
Don't add a `border-left` or `border-right` over 1px as a colored accent stripe. Use a full border, a background tint, or a leading icon.
Don't use gradient text (`background-clip: text`). Emphasis is weight or size.
Don't add colors beyond the named status set. Delete red stays on destructive controls; status colors stay on dots and badges, never surfaces.
Don't build identical card grids; cards have structure because their content varies.
Don't reach for a modal first. Inline expansion, collapsibles, and contextual panels usually serve better.
Don't use `transition: all`. Transition colours via `--swap`; move things with `transform`/`opacity`, and change height only through `expand`, `autoHeight`, or `morphHeight`.
Don't let content pop in, jump, or blank out. A new state arrives through a transition, a list change moves rows rather than replacing them, and a refresh updates in place.
Don't use bounce, elastic, or overshoot easing, or durations over 260ms for anything but chart data morphs (350ms).
Don't slide whole pages sideways between tabs or let the old and new page overlap at full strength; fade through.
Don't hold the page frozen waiting for data; cap `settle` at about 50ms and let late content ease in.
Don't use `word-break: break-word` or `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on headings or labels: inside a flex row they split words to make room. Use `overflow-wrap: break-word`.
